implementation_statement: POL-02 Access Control Policy was approved 2026-08-31 (P06). Supporting procedures (seasonal onboarding, access review) are due 2026-11-30.

Accounts are created in the identity provider from HR tickets and federated to the tax software, portal staff console, and productivity suite. Gaps: seasonal accounts are disabled about 6 business days after the season ends; no quarterly access review; the shared intake mailbox has a password known to 6 staff.
Tax software roles (preparer, reviewer, e-file coordinator, admin) and DMS folder permissions by practice area enforce access. Cloud tenant roles are assigned to 2 named IT administrators.
Standard users have no local admin rights. Gaps: 3 partners hold standing global administrator rights on everyday productivity suite accounts; all tax staff can open every client folder in the DMS.
evidence: Admin role report; DMS permission export

implementation_statement: The identity provider locks accounts for 15 minutes after 10 failed attempts. The portal vendor applies its own lockout for client accounts.
Screen lock after 10 minutes is enforced on managed endpoints. Gap: 4 seasonal stations at the Branch office are excluded so preparers can share them.
The tax software ends idle sessions after 30 minutes and the portal after 15 minutes (vendor settings confirmed).
Remote access to the DMS uses the cloud VPN gateway with SSO and MFA. Gap: the MSP remote management tool has unrestricted access to all endpoints with no source restriction.
Awareness and training rules are in POL-05 (P06). Procedures for seasonal staff are due 2026-11-30.
Annual security training each December. Gaps: no phishing exercises; no content on business email compromise or refund diversion; seasonal preparers start before completing training.
Planned: role-based training for preparers and client service staff on call-back verification and IRC 7216 consent rules, before the 2027 filing season.

implementation_statement: Gap: logs are never reviewed. Planned: log workspace with alerting on bulk downloads, new inbox rules, and impossible travel; monthly review by the Qualified Individual starting 2026-12.
Tax software vendor retains activity logs for the contract term. Gap: identity and mailbox logs keep only the default 30 to 90 days.
Audit record generation is on by default in the SaaS systems and cloud tenant.
A control assessment was performed 2026-08-03 to 2026-08-07 by an independent assessor (P07).
Weaknesses are tracked in the P07 POA&M with owners and dates, reviewed monthly by the Firm Administrator.
Planned: quarterly metrics to the Firm Administrator and the annual written report to the Partner Group (first report 2026-10-20).

implementation_statement: Gap: no penetration test has ever been performed. Planned: external and internal test by an independent firm in 2026-11, then annually, scoped from the risk assessment (314.4(d)(2)(i)).
A standard laptop image exists. Gap: no documented baseline for firewalls, the VPN gateway, or cloud workloads.
Gap: no change management procedure. Planned: change log with approval by the IT Manager (MSP changes) and Firm Administrator (major changes), from 2026-12.
Endpoint settings are enforced by device management. Gap: cloud VM and firewall hardening is not documented.
Endpoints are inventoried in device management. Gap: printer-scanners, network devices, and SaaS services are not in one inventory.
Gap: no contingency plan. The BIA (P05) was approved 2026-08-31; the plan, including a deadline contingency procedure, is due 2027-03-31.
One DMS restore test was performed in 2025. Gap: the audit workpaper server has never been restore-tested; no test schedule.
The DMS and workpaper servers are backed up daily to an immutable vault in a second region under a separate backup administrator role. SaaS data is backed up by each vendor.
Recovery procedures will be written into the contingency plan due 2027-03-31.
All staff sign in with unique accounts through the identity provider. Gap: the shared intake mailbox and 3 other service mailboxes still accept legacy authentication without MFA.
MFA is required for administrators. Gap: administrators use push approval without number matching; phishing-resistant keys are planned.
MFA (push) is required for all staff on every federated application. Gap: push without number matching is open to MFA fatigue attacks.
Minimum length 14 and a banned-password list are enforced. Gaps: the shared intake mailbox password is shared by 6 staff and unchanged since 2024; local admin passwords are not unique.
Clients authenticate to the portal with a password; MFA is offered but optional (38% enrolled).
POL-03 Incident Response Policy approved 2026-08-31 (P06).
Incidents have been handled ad hoc by the IT Manager and MSP. The BEC and data theft runbook (P08) was approved 2026-08-31; the first tabletop is due 2026-12-15.
Planned: security category in the IT ticketing system to log and track every incident.
External reporting duties (FTC, IRS Stakeholder Liaison, next-business-day e-file report, states) are defined in the P08 matrix. Gap: staff have not been told how to report internally.
The written incident response plan is POL-03 plus the P08 runbook, which together cover the seven areas in 314.4(h)(1)-(7).
Paper is shredded by a vendor with certificates. Gaps: printer-scanner drives are not wiped at lease end; retired laptop drives are wiped without a record.
Both offices use badge entry; the Main office server and network closet is locked with 3 key holders.

implementation_statement: Risk acceptance levels are set in POL-01 and P01. Gap: first written risk assessment; no report to the Partner Group yet.
Background checks for all hires, including seasonal preparers, before start.
HR emails IT at termination. Gap: no same-day disable requirement; seasonal staff are disabled late.
All staff sign a confidentiality agreement at hire. Gap: it does not mention IRC 7216 and 6713 penalties, and seasonal preparers sign on day one after system access is granted.
The TPCP is categorized Moderate (section 6 of this SSP).
Written risk assessment completed 2026-07-24 using NIST SP 800-30 Rev. 1 (P01), with the 314.4(b)(1) criteria. Annual update each July.
Gap: vulnerability scanning is ad hoc (last 2025-03). Planned: monthly authenticated internal scans and external scans by the MSP from 2026-11, exceeding the six-month minimum in 314.4(d)(2)(ii).
Contracts with the tax software, portal, and cloud vendors include confidentiality and security terms. Gaps: the MSP contract has none; the AI extraction sub-processor terms were not reviewed.
The tax software vendor's SOC 2 Type 2 report was reviewed 2026-08 (P09). Gaps: no service provider inventory; no periodic assessment of the MSP, portal, or practice management vendors.
Firewalls at both offices; site-to-site VPN to the cloud tenant; no inbound services exposed except the VPN gateway.
TLS 1.2 or higher for the tax software, portal, and e-file transmission; IPsec between offices and cloud. Gap: returns and source documents are emailed to clients as plain attachments on request.
Encryption keys are managed by the providers' key management services, per their SOC 2 system descriptions.
Providers use industry-standard encryption (AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.2+ in transit) per their SOC 2 system descriptions.
SaaS and cloud storage are encrypted at rest by the providers; laptops use full-disk encryption. Gaps: 12 desktops are unencrypted; printer-scanners store images unencrypted.
OS patches install automatically on endpoints; the MSP patches cloud VMs monthly. Gap: VPN gateway and firewall firmware are updated ad hoc.
EDR on all endpoints and cloud VMs, managed by the MSP.
EDR alerts are watched by the MSP during business hours. Gaps: no after-hours monitoring; no monitoring of mailbox rules, sign-in anomalies, or bulk downloads.
Gap: no retention and disposal schedule; files go back to 2009. Planned: schedule approved by 2026-12-31 and first disposal run by 2027-06-30 (314.4(c)(6)).
Planned: annual assessment of the MSP and the tax software vendor, using SOC 2 reports or a questionnaire (P09).
Office Wi-Fi uses WPA2-Enterprise tied to the identity provider for staff; client and guest Wi-Fi is on a separate network with no route to firm systems.
